key_insight: An augmented block preconditioner enables robust iterative solution of fully coupled, two-phase incompressible inductionless MHD systems.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports three-dimensional conducting-fluid simulations with discontinuous material properties and challenging coupled flow–current dynamics.
method: Discretize current density, velocity, electric potential and pressure using high-order, charge-conservative ALE finite elements and backward Euler time stepping.
Add grad-div stabilization to the current-density and momentum equations.
Combine augmented Lagrangian techniques with approximate block factorization, then solve using preconditioned FGMRES.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments confirm high-order accuracy and discrete charge conservation; a heavy-fluid-drop benchmark demonstrates preconditioner robustness to material-property discontinuities and mesh size.
watch_item: The abstract gives no quantitative iteration counts or runtime scaling, limiting assessment of computational efficiency.
paper_title: Robust augmented Block Preconditioning for two-phase Incompressible Inductionless MHD
